problems.problem: Two members' words are kept verbatim without consent, under the label 'summarized'. This fails G9 and therefore fidelity. Priya's whole interest is stored word for word ('fear and anxiety outcomes, and whether the results can be pooled'), and Jamal's records keep runs of 6 to 8 of his words, although he asked for summaries. Both texts also went into the Individual Motivation decision that was certified.
problems.cause: Kit: record_interest() never checks consent; its docstring says 'in their words', and its refusal asks for the member's 'own words'. answer() checks only the verbatim flag and never compares the text with what the member said. Prompt: the privacy section says 'only in your own words' but gives no test, and short answers make copying easy.
problems.fix: Kit: add said=<the member's message> to answer() and record_interest(). For a summaries-only member, refuse any text that shares 5 or more consecutive words with that message (case-insensitive), saying 'Put this in your own words'. Change the record_interest docstring to 'verbatim only with consent; otherwise your own summary'. Prompt, privacy section: add 'A summary uses no run of five or more of the member's words; for a short answer, name its subject in different words (e.g., Priya: mainly the emotional outcomes, and whether results can be combined statistically).'

problems.problem: The Step 3 reply was overwhelming and unannounced. Msg 26's Next line promised only to 'tell you what Step 3 will check'. Msg 28 then delivered four full search cards, a tag key, a 10-row table, a coverage DRAFT, an end-date line and a 14-item Sources line: about 1,500 rendered words, 358 of them prose against a 180-word cap. Satisfaction fell to 3, and the persona wrote 'we hadn't asked to see any of it'.
problems.cause: Prompt 2d ('When the Team's Purpose is certified, say in one line what Step 3 will check') does not announce that searches will run. Step 3 asks for two searches per source, each with a full card. The kit renders four separate cards.
problems.fix: Prompt 2d: in the reply that asks for the Team's Purpose certification, the Next line says 'Next: I'll search PubMed and OpenAlex for existing reviews of your topic and focus and show you what I find.' Step 3: 'Show one card per source; in it, the topic and focus strings each sit in their own code block, block rows appear once, and the focus card adds only its new block and the combined count.' Kit: add k.search_report(paired=True), and print a one-line tag key covering only the tags used. Rubric: add a diagnostic for rendered words including tables (target 600 or fewer).

problems.problem: The search end dates are partly misstated. The FACT line '17 of the 46 state none' rests only on abstracts; the code counted 'search_end_not_in_abstract'. Row 10's '2022' comes from 'published between 2017 and 2022', an inclusion window, not a search end date. The separate line '1 April 2024 · 2 September 2025 ...' reads as dates (1 April 2024) rather than 'row 1: April 2024'.
problems.cause: Kit: the end-date extractor accepts publication-window phrases, the summary wording turns 'unknown' into 'none', and review_table puts the dates on a separate numbered line instead of a 'Search end' column, which the prompt asks for.
problems.fix: Kit: accept only search phrases (searched, search was conducted, through, up to, until, from inception to); flag 'published between' as 'window, not search end'. Write 'unknown (not in the abstract)' for the rest, and render a 'Search end' column in review_table. Prompt Step 3: add 'Never say a review states no search end date when only its abstract was read; write unknown.'

problems.problem: Example replies favor particular options in choice questions. During the scope conflict, msg 14's examples are 'Priya: 1. a.' (keep the needle topic) and 'Jamal: 1. c'. Neither shows b, Jamal's own position, although the reply says 'I won't take a side'. Msg 16's example '1. Keep 4 to 12. 2. Fear and anxiety.' was copied almost word for word by the team (msg 17). Msgs 10 and 28 show 'a.' as the example.
problems.cause: Prompt item 6 asks for 'one or two example replies' but does not require them to stay neutral. Only msgs 20 and 22 used placeholders.
problems.fix: Prompt item 6: add 'When a question offers options, the example shows only the reply format with placeholders (e.g., "Priya: 1. <a, b or c>, because ..."), never a particular option, least of all in a disagreement.'

problems.problem: The Waiting-on-you count follows no single rule. Msg 8 counts per member ('9'). Msg 14 shows '2' for a question asked of 'each of you' plus a conditional one. Msg 18 shows '1 (Maya, Jamal, Priya)' for a confirmation asked of each member. The persona was confused twice: 'keeps changing (9, then 3, then 1, then 2)' and 'says 1 but names all three'. The same issue was reported in the previous round.
problems.cause: Kit: status_line counts ask records times items and ignores the number of people asked. The prompt says to count 'the answers ... with who gives them' but gives no way to mark a question as asked of each member.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.ask(..., each=True), count items times addressees for such asks, and print 'Waiting on you: 3 answers (Maya, Jamal, Priya)'. Prompt, status line: 'A question asked of each member counts once per member; name each person once.'

problems.problem: A whole reply (msg 18) went on asking all three members to re-confirm a focus wording whose only new parts came from Maya and Priya themselves (msg 17). Only Jamal needed to confirm. This took the first literature FACT to the very limit of the pace allowance (turn 12 of 12) and pushed the kinds of purpose, which the script expected at msg 16, back to msg 20.
problems.cause: Prompt 2b says 'Gather all pending changes to the focus into one question for the other members' but does not say that this question can share a reply with the kinds of purpose, or that it goes only to members who did not make the change.
problems.fix: Prompt 2b: add 'Ask that question only of members who did not make the change, as item 1 of the reply that shows the kinds of purpose and the motivation draft; do not spend a reply on it.'

problems.problem: Jargon a novice team cannot decode sits outside the prose. Msg 28 has an unexplained 'PMID' column, 'narrative review' and 'need a free access code from OpenAlex'; the persona could not tell whether it had to act on the last one. The plan map (msgs 8, 26) has 'extraction form, property registry and atlas', 'stopping rule' and 'protocol and registration', never explained.
problems.cause: The kit's plan_map and review_table labels carry no glosses. Prompt R14's list of terms to explain at first use leaves out PMID, narrative review, scoping review and protocol. Prompt 2d allows mentioning the access code without asking for it.
problems.fix: Kit: review_table header 'PubMed number (PMID)'; plan_map glosses ('a form for what to record from each study', 'a list of study features to track', 'a map of the evidence', 'when to stop searching', 'the written plan, and recording it in a public register'). Prompt R14: add PMID, narrative review, scoping review and protocol to the first-use list. Step 3: 'Mention the OpenAlex access code only as a numbered request naming who gets it and how; otherwise write "I read the first 100 by relevance".'

problems.problem: The team never learned what certifying commits it to. Self-reports at msgs 9, 11, 15, 25 and 27 say 'not sure what certify means' and 'did not follow why ... need two separate certifications'. The prompt-mandated 'approve (certify)' gloss at msg 8 was not enough.
problems.cause: Prompt Certifying section: the reviewer is told how to certify, never what it means or why Step 2 has two decisions.
problems.fix: Prompt Certifying: with the first CERTIFY line, add one plain sentence outside it: 'Certifying means you, as the named reviewer, approve this decision and say why; later steps build on it, and it changes only if the team agrees to reopen it. Step 2 has two: what each of you gets from the review, and what the review is for.'

problems.problem: The 'When convenient' line asks a novice team to type a contact email for PubMed. This puts an email address in the chat for no benefit. The persona asked 'why would PubMed need it, and do we have to give one?'.
problems.cause: Prompt 2d makes the email request mandatory during set-up, and kit setup() always adds it as an optional item.
problems.fix: Prompt 2d: 'Ask for a contact email only if PubMed refuses or slows a search (a logged error); then add "optional; searches work without it".' Kit setup(): leave the email out of when_convenient unless an NCBI error has been logged.

problems.problem: A paragraph of the agent's own synthesis is labeled 'JUDGMENT:', and it overstates the members: 'All three of you now share Maya's team purpose', although Priya had said 'mostly' (msg 11).
problems.cause: Prompt R2 defines JUDGMENT as supplied by a named member, but 2b's reflection guidance leads the agent to label team-level statements as JUDGMENT too.
problems.fix: Prompt R2: add 'Label JUDGMENT only statements where each clause names its member and keeps their qualifiers (e.g., "Jamal: yes; Priya: mostly"); a sentence you compose about the team as a whole is DRAFT.'

judge.strengths: The scripted moments were handled well, and the fidelity failure comes from the copied wording described under G9, not from any one scripted moment. Moment 3: the agent asked once whether Maya's purpose stood for Jamal and for Priya. Moment 5: it reported the scope conflict with each side's words, linked it to the answers that depend on the needle topic, and left the decision to the team. Moment 7: Priya's question about existing reviews was answered as unknown until Step 3, with no papers named. Moment 8: [tiab] and * were explained in the tag key before the strings appeared, and Jamal's question got a three-line answer followed by 'Still open'. Each change to the topic or focus was reconciled, so the focus is built entirely from members' words and 'Added by me: nothing' is true each time it appears. Search transparency was complete: four cards with exact strings, counts per block, date bounds, Sources and a 'Left out on purpose' table, and every number verified against saved responses by hash. Both certifications are clean: a listed reviewer, her own reasons, the certified wording identical to what she was shown, a commit for each. Prose stayed under 180 words in 12 of 13 turns. Diagnostics: D1, D2, D5, D6, D8, D9 and D10 are all 0; D4 is 1 (msg 12); D7 is 1 of the 1 places reached so far. One log record was corrected by appending a new record (L000128) rather than editing the old one. The git identity is neutral, and no email address or key is stored. Workspace checked: <scratch>/sim/r5/p2_rc5/stir-l4-workspace (log/actions.jsonl, plan/plan.yaml, plan/team.yaml, data/derived/step3_summary.json, data/derived/step3_review_records.csv, data/manifest.csv).
